items.title: Conrad "Connie" Jones Interview, 1981-09-01
items.q: And he did an awful lot for me and an awful lot for other people too. He's responsible for a lot of people being in the music business today.

ctx.x: Yeah. But he was an important grown man in your eyes. Oh yes, oh yeah.

Well he had that mystique, he was a musician, a professional musician too. A guy that did it all the time. But we later spoke about, you know, I told him about how I used to listen to him when I was a kid and played. He couldn't even get a kick out of that. Tony was genuinely nice. He was just one of the most giving people that I've ever met in my life. He was just a warm, friendly, just a good man. And he did an awful lot for me and an awful lot for other people too. He's responsible for a lot of people being in…
Yeah. Well, Nina Piconi is really not Nina. Never Tony though, huh? No, not that I can remember. But for a long time it was Mr. El Morico. Of course, the days were different in those days.

items.title: Conrad "Connie" Jones Interview, 1981-07-23, 08-03
items.q: When the junior band, Tony Amarico's, I forget the circumstances.

ctx.x: Yeah. Well, and we mentioned Paul Whiteman, but never did he get to that TV show very much. He just barely mentioned it last time I think. What happened with the TV show? How about that?

Let me see, let me put this together. When the junior band, Tony Amarico's, I forget the circumstances. If I'm not mistaken, we had done a couple of Nord TV shows. And TV was pretty hot stuff in those days. I think we only had one channel then, WDSU. And some kind of way or another, we were in some kind of a battle of the bands. And we were chosen to be the band to go to the Paul Whiteman show. Not as contestants. We did not go as contestants. Just as a feature. And we made the trip to Philadelphia by train. And…
